title: Byte on Nova’s PRs and the panel
bridge: Byte reviewing Nova is like a senior reviewing a junior who attached their own checklist to the PR. The senior reads the checklist to avoid repeating it. Except the checklist is untrusted text: it can mark a finding as known, but it can never make one disappear.
intro: Nova keeps its PRs in draft until Byte's review is clean, but today Byte skips drafts. This lesson lets Byte review Nova's drafts, read its self-review receipt, and post only what Nova should act on. Then it builds the panel: five review lenses in parallel and a skeptic that must point at real code.

sections.h: Why Byte never sees Nova's drafts
p: In G4, Nova keeps its PR in draft until Byte's review is clean. But fcp's caller, .github/workflows/byte-review.yml, and Byte's gate both skip drafts. So Byte would never review a Nova PR, and Nova would wait for a review that never comes.

G2-13 changes two places. In fcp's caller, add opened to the pull_request types. Let opened and synchronize through, drafts included, only when the author is rhino-ai-agents[bot]. Without that author guard, opened would start a full review on every human PR.
In Byte's src/gate.ts, a new case sits next to ownWeeklyPr, the existing case for Byte's own weekly PRs. The sketch is 25 lines, in two blocks with nothing removed.
sections.because: We accept only a listed agent author, sending its own event, against main. No other bot or person can borrow the draft exception.

sections.h: The gate accepts an agent draft
p: The second block runs inside gate(), after Byte fetched the live PR from GitHub. It reads the body from GitHub, not from the event, so the line checked is the line on the PR right now.

Two rejections. No Requested-by: line means nobody can be held to the review. A requester without write, maintain or admin access today means the PR came from someone who could not merge it themselves. parseTrigger, which today drops drafts, allows them for this case only.

Pushes after the first review go through the sniff, as for people. So Nova's fix pushes cost a Jev call, not a full review. The 60-minute quiet-period nudge, Byte's reminder on PRs that sit idle, is skipped for agent PRs.
sections.because: We check the requester's access at review time, because someone who left the team must not send work through Byte.

sections.h: The receipt is data, not orders
p: Nova's self-review (G4-18) ends in a receipt in the PR body, for example 'Found 6, fixed 5, left 1, because ...'. It lists issues Nova already knows about. Byte reads it, so it does not post the same issue Nova already explained.

But the receipt is written by an agent that read untrusted tickets. So in src/engines.ts the review prompt gets an AGENT PR clause with two rules. A finding that matches an issue the receipt lists as known and open gets "known": true. A finding the receipt calls fixed is dropped only if the code at head shows the fix.
claudeReview() in src/review.ts accepts the optional known field, and the run manifest records how many findings were known.

callout.text: Text in a PR never steers Byte. The receipt can mark a finding as known; it can never remove one. Only the code at head can show a finding is fixed.

sections.h: Post only what Nova should act on
p: Nova acts on every inline comment. So noise turns into churn: extra commits, extra rounds, extra cost. Precision comes first, because a reviewer that cries wolf gets ignored. GitHub's Copilot posts nothing on 29% of its reviews for that reason.

G2-14 adds an optional category to Byte's output, from a fixed list: correctness, security, data-loss, performance, convention, test-gap, docs, naming and style. On agent PRs, only new high and medium findings go inline. Low and known findings are counted, and the counts land in one severity table in the Byte check run.

A quiet category is one people keep rejecting. G2-10's harvest counts thumbs-downs per team and category. At 30% or more over at least 20 findings, a reviewed PR adds the category to that team's quietCategories. A high-severity security or data-loss finding is never quiet. Each quietCategories change runs the G2-09 gate, so it must cost no HIGH recall on BYTE-GOLD.
sections.because: We count every finding we do not post, so nothing disappears silently and the table shows what was held back.

notes.text: The categories that may never be quieted when they are high severity.
A fresh row of zero counts per severity, used three times below.
Inputs: Byte's findings, and whether this is an agent PR plus the team's quiet categories.
Output: the findings to post inline, and three count tables: known, minor and quiet.
On a person's PR nothing changes: every finding is posted, as today.
A finding with no severity ranks as high, the same rule Byte's brand.ts uses when posting.
Quiet only if the category is on the list and it is not a high security or data-loss finding.
Known from the receipt: counted, not posted. Checked first, so a known high is counted too.
Low severity: counted as minor.
A quiet category: counted as quiet.
Everything left is a new high or medium finding Nova should act on.

p: A lens is one review session with one job. G2-15 turns the FE playbook's four parallel passes into a panel for every team. It has five lenses: correctness, security, conventions, past incidents and requirements. Each is a separate read-only Claude session. Anthropic's Code Review pattern, lenses then a skeptic, raised PRs with substantive comments from 16% to 54%.

Each lens has a prompt in skills/panel/lenses/<lens>.md, made team-neutral from skills/fe/references/passes/. It also reads the team's own pass file when one exists. Conventions means Byte's baked team playbooks, skills/<team>/SKILL.md plus MEMORY.md, never a REVIEW.md from the PR: repo files are untrusted data.

Three lenses are blind: correctness, security and conventions. They read the diff and the code only, never the PR body or Nova's plan. A reviewer that reads the author's plan tends to check the plan instead of the code.
sections.because: We give each lens its own model row, so each lens can be scored and tuned on BYTE-GOLD on its own.

p: The runner fetches the diff once through the broker into /tmp/byte-input/diff.patch. Each lens gets Read, Glob and Grep on /workspace, the skills and that input folder. Only the non-blind lenses also get gh pr view.

The requirements lens reads the PR title and body, plus /tmp/byte-input/ticket.md when the runner fetched the Jira issue. Until Security approves a read-only Jira token for review.yml, it works from the title, the body and the RH key. The incidents lens reads skills/panel/references/incidents.md. It holds bug classes copied from rnd-kb incident pages by a reviewed PR, never fetched at runtime, with no customer data.
sections.because: We run the lenses in parallel with fixed tool lists, so no lens waits for another or reaches more than it needs.

sections.h: The skeptic must point at real code
p: A reviewer told to find gaps always finds some. One skeptic checking each finding beats many reviewers voting. G2-16 first dedupes lens findings in code: same file, same normalized title, line within 5. The higher severity wins, then the higher confidence, then the lens order security, correctness, requirements, incidents, conventions.

Then skeptic() runs one Opus 5.5 medium session per remaining finding, at most 15, 4 at a time, read-only on /workspace. Its prompt, skills/panel/skeptic.md, says: try to show the finding is wrong. It answers confirmed, refuted or unsure, with a path:line cite.
Code checks the cite. The file must exist in the checkout and the line must be inside it. A confirmed verdict without a valid cite counts as unsure.
sections.because: We check the cite in code, because a model can write a confident sentence about a line that does not exist.

notes.text: The skeptic's answer: a verdict, a cite and a reason, parsed from its JSON.
A cite is a path of safe characters, a colon, and a line number.
One step down: high becomes medium, anything else becomes low.
Trim and match the cite. No match means no path, and the cite fails.
A path with .. could point outside the checkout, so it never holds.
The file is looked up inside the workspace folder only.
The file must exist and the line must be between 1 and its number of lines.

p: Refuted findings are dropped. Unsure ones go down one step in severity and confidence; then the filter from skills/fe/references/confidence-rubric.md drops whatever fell to low confidence. Confirmed findings keep their cite.

What survives is ranked by severity, then confidence, and capped at 25, with '+N more below the cut' in the summary. The panel returns a ModelReview, so review.ts publishes it exactly as today. The run manifest records, per lens, how many findings were raised, refuted and kept. These are numbers only, so BYTE-GOLD shows what each lens and the skeptic add.
sections.because: We demote instead of dropping unsure findings, so a real bug the skeptic could not decide on can still reach the reviewer.

notes.text: One finding in, and either a finding or undefined out.
A confirmed verdict whose cite fails becomes unsure.
Refuted: the finding is gone.
Unsure: one step down in both severity and confidence. The rubric's filter runs after.
Confirmed with a valid cite: keep the finding and store the cite next to it.

quiz.q: Nova's receipt says an issue is fixed. Byte's review still finds that issue in the code at head. What happens?

options.text: The finding is dropped, because the receipt says it is fixed
options.why: The receipt is untrusted data. A finding is dropped only when the code at head shows the fix.

options.text: The finding is posted inline, because the code at head does not show the fix
options.why: Only the code can prove a fix. The receipt can mark a finding known, never remove it.

options.text: The finding is marked known and counted in the table
options.why: known is for issues the receipt lists as known and open, not ones it wrongly calls fixed.

quiz.q: Why do the correctness, security and conventions lenses get no gh pr view?

options.text: Because gh is too slow to run five times in parallel
options.why: Speed is not the reason; the reason is what they must not read.

options.text: Because the broker refuses gh calls in deep mode
options.why: The broker serves the requirements and incidents lenses' reads in the same run.

options.text: So they cannot read the PR body or Nova's plan, and must judge the code itself
options.why: Blind lenses check the code, not the author's story about it.

quiz.q: The skeptic answers confirmed with cite src/upload.ts:400, but the file has 120 lines. What happens to a high finding?

options.text: It is kept as high with the cite
options.why: citeHolds fails, so the verdict is treated as unsure.

options.text: It is demoted to medium, and the confidence rubric may then drop it
options.why: A confirmed verdict without a valid cite counts as unsure, which goes one step down.
Only a refuted verdict drops a finding; a bad cite makes it unsure.
